answer: Approximately **5.6% (1 of 18) of the original studies in the Experimental Economics (ee) replication project were conducted in the United Kingdom.** The single UK-original is study **ee.13 — "Deferred compensation in multiperiod labor contracts: an experimental test of Lazear's model"** (Discipline: Economics; Published 2011 in *The American Economic Review*; `experiment_country.o = "United Kingdom"`). The remaining 17 ee originals were conducted in the United States (11), Germany (2), Switzerland (2), Australia (1), and Austria (1). The proportion is the unweighted share of studies (1/18 ≈ 0.0556, 5.5556%); it is not weighted by sample size.

payload.hypothesis: Approximately 5.6% (1 out of 18) of the original studies in the Experimental Economics (ee) project were conducted in the United Kingdom.
payload.workflow: Loaded data/meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows × 57 cols). Subset to project=='ee', yielding 18 rows with 18 unique ids and 0 missing experiment_country.o. Applied a defensive, case-and-whitespace-insensitive UK label rule with equivalence set {united kingdom, uk, gb, great britain, england, scotland, wales, northern ireland, united kingdom of great britain and northern ireland}; empirically only 'United Kingdom' matched. Numerator = 1 (study ee.13), denominator = 18 (ee rows = unique studies, no weighting by n.o), giving 1/18 ≈ 0.0556 (5.5556%). drop==True filter was NOT applied; for transparency, 0 ee rows are flagged drop==True. The replication-success CSV was inspected but contains no country column and was not used.
